rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasāṣa means need or want; its root evokes gaps in a house, likening poverty to an enclosure with openings that cannot meet its needs.
rows.anchor: أصلها خصاص البيت وهي فرجة شبه حالة الفقر والحاجة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says unfillable poverty is called khasāṣa, as it is also called khalla; a khas is a reed-and-branch hut named for its gaps.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب عبر عن الفقر الذي لا يسد بالخصاصة كما عبر عنه بالخلة والخص بيت من قصب وشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet distributed Banū Naḍīr property among the Emigrants, except for three needy Ansār: Abū Dujāna, Sahl b. Ḥunayf, and al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣimma.
rows.anchor: وكان عليه السلام قسم أموال بني النضير على المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار إلا ثلاثة نفر محتاجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate report says only Sahl and Abū Dujāna received shares, since al-Ḥārith b. al-Ṣimma had died at Biʾr Maʿūna.
rows.anchor: وروي لم يعط إلا رجلين سهلا وأبا دجانة فإن الحارث بن الصمة قتل في بئر معونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet offered the Ansār a choice of sharing their homes and wealth with the Emigrants and sharing the spoils, or keeping their property without a share; they chose to give their property and the spoils to the Emigrants.
rows.anchor: فقالت : الأنصار بل نقسم لهم من أموالنا وديارنا ونؤثرهم بالغنيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet kept some land for his own cultivation and later had the Emigrants return the palm groves the Ansār had lent them for their fruit, since the Ansār no longer needed them and had never transferred ownership.
rows.anchor: وكان عليه السلام أعطى بعض الأراضي وأبقى بعضها يزرع له ولما أعطى المهاجرين أمرهم برد ما كان للأنصار

rows.speaker: أنس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: An Anṣārī in hardship received a sheep's head and passed it among seven households, each considering a neighbor more needy, until it returned to him.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه أنه قال : أهدي لرجل من الأنصار رأس شاة وكان مجهودا

rows.speaker: حذيفة العدوي
rows.claim: At Yarmūk, Ḥudhayfa al-ʿAdawī offered water to his wounded cousin; the cousin directed him to Hishām b. al-ʿĀṣ, who passed him to another wounded man, and all three died before drinking.
rows.anchor: قال حذيفة العدوي انطلقت يوم اليرموك أطلب ابن عم لي ومعي شيء من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving up one's own life for another is a form of self-preference and exceeds preferring another with one's wealth.
rows.anchor: وهذا من قبيل الإيثار بالنفس وهو فوق الإيثار بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuḥḥ combines miserliness with greed, two blameworthy traits of the self; it is attributed to the self because it is an innate impulse toward withholding.
rows.anchor: والشح بالضم والكسر بخل مع حرص فيكون جامعا بين ذميمتين من صفات النفس وإضافته إلى النفس لأنه غريزة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being protected from one's avarice by God's enabling means resisting the self's love of wealth and aversion to spending.
rows.anchor: أي ومن يوق بتوفيق الله شحها حتى يخالفها فيما يغلب عليها من حب المال وبغض الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful are those who attain every desired good and escape every harm; falāḥ is happiness in both abodes.
rows.anchor: الفائزون بكل مطلوب الناجون من كل مكروه والفلاح اسم لسعادة الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The success clause is an aside praising the Ansār, since the qualities just described are their virtues and refined states.
rows.anchor: والجملة اعتراض وارد لمدح الأنصار والثناء عليهم فإن الفتوى هي الأوصاف المذكورة في حقهم

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet called love of the Ansār a sign of faith and hatred of them a sign of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : آية الإيمان حب الأنصار وآية النفاق بغض الأنصار

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that God forgive the Ansār, their children, and their grandchildren.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : اللهم اغفر للأنصار ولأبناء الأنصار وأبناء أبناء الأنصار

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says innate generosity opposes avarice, which is among the self's inherent traits; God promises success to the person who spends and gives.
rows.anchor: قال السهروردي في العوارف : السخاء صفة غريزية في مقابلة الشح والشح من لوازم صفة النفس

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet counted obedient avarice among three ruinous traits: avarice is destructive when obeyed, while its mere presence is natural to the earthly self.
rows.anchor: والنبي عليه السلام نبه بقوله ثلاث مهلكات وثلاث منجيات فجعل إحدى المهلكات شحا مطاعا

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī distinguishes innate sakha from acquired jud: every innately generous person gives generously, but not every generous giver has sakha; Sufis' sakha prompts giving and altruism.
rows.anchor: والسخاء أتم وأكمل من الجود وفي مقابلة الجود البخل وفي مقابلة السخاء الشح

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says God is not described by sakha, which arises from innate dispositions; acquired generosity may seek display or reward, while true sakha is free of recompense and belongs to the people of purity.
rows.anchor: والحق تعالى لا يوصف بالسخاء لأن السخاء من نتيجة الغرائز والله تعالى منزه عن الغريزة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says shuḥḥ means committing sins, as though one were miserly with obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن رحمه الله : الشح هو العمل بالمعاصي كأنه يشح بالطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition of shuḥḥ is letting one's gaze covet what does not belong to oneself.
rows.anchor: فدخل فيه ما قيل الشح أن تطمح عين الرجل إلى ما ليس له

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet described looking at another man's woman as shuḥḥ; the source links it to withholding the gaze and chastity and says such a person does not prosper.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : من الشح نظرك إلى امرأة غيرك

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba reportedly derived al-Muhaymin as a diminutive of muʾmin, with the hamza changed to hāʾ; the author says this approaches unbelief by abandoning reverence.
rows.anchor: قتيبة لما قال في المهيمن أنه مصغر من مؤمن

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī defines God's name al-Muhaymin as His oversight of creation's deeds, provisions, and lifespans through knowledge, complete dominion, and preservation; only God possesses all three absolutely, and the name is said to occur in ancient scriptures.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام الغزالي رحمه الله معنى المهيمن في حق الله أنه القائم على خلقه بأعمالهم وأرزاقهم وآجالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant of al-Muhaymin witnesses God as guardian over everything and gives each person their due; the knower of this name monitors the heart and limbs, guards against Satan, and watches over God's servants, becoming humble and vigilant before God.
rows.anchor: وعبد المهيمن هو الذي شاهد كون الحق رقيبا شهيدا على كل شيء فهو يرقب نفسه وغيره بإيفاء حق كل ذي حق عليه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: When Ibrāhīm b. Adham sat with legs extended while praying, a voice rebuked him: this is how one sits in the presence of kings.
rows.anchor: حكي أن إبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله كان يصلي قاعدا فجلس ومد رجليه فهتف به هاتف

rows.speaker: الحريري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī would not stretch his legs even in solitude; when told no one could see him, he replied that keeping proper manners with God matters more.
rows.anchor: وإن الحريري كان لا يمد رجليه في الخلوة فقيل له : ليس يراك أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recounts leaning against the Maqām Ibrāhīm after circumambulating the Kaaba and receiving a divine rebuke about distance amid nearness; he then stayed by the Kaaba's door in the front row during his Meccan residence.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير يقرب من هذا ما وقع لي عند الكعبة فإني بعدما طفت بالبيت استندت إلى مقام إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muhaymin especially signifies oversight of inward states and secrets.
rows.anchor: وخاصة هذا الاسم الإشراف على البواطن والأسرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting this name one hundred times after ablution and prayer, in retreat with focused attention, is said to bring the reciter what they seek.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأه مائة مرة بعد الغسل والصلاة في خلوة بجمع خاطر نال ما أراد

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: The Idrīsī invocation calls God Knower of the Unseen, whose knowledge misses nothing and is never burdened; al-Suhrawardī says persevering in it strengthens memory and removes forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وفي الأربعين الإدريسية يا علام الغيوب فلا يفوت شيء من علمه ولا يؤوده قال السهرودي من داوم عليه قوي حفظه وذهب نسيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means prevailing in judgment or bestowing honor.
rows.anchor: غالب در حكم يا بخشنده عزت

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the names as indicating God's oneness in essence and attributes, wise governance, transcendence from contingent defects, bringing things from nonexistence into being, preserving them, honoring friends, subduing enemies, manifesting majesty in all forms, and transcending all association.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية قوله سبحانه هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الملك الخ يشير إلى وحدانية ذاته وفردانية صفاته

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqli's ʿArāʾis reads associating partners with God through the eyes and thoughts as what the declaration of divine transcendence excludes.
rows.anchor: وفي عرائس البقلي سبحان الله عما يشركون إليه بالنواظر والخواطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khāliq means the measurer of things according to wisdom and will; the root's original sense is measurement, as in shaping a shoe to a measure, whether creation uses material or not.
rows.anchor: أصل معنى الخلق التقدير كما يقال خلق النعل إذا قدرها وسواها بمقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant of al-Khāliq measures things according to God's intent because the divine attribute of creating and measuring is disclosed to him; he plans only by God's determination.
rows.anchor: وعبد الخالق هو الذي يقدر الأشياء على وفق مراد الحق لتجليه له بوصف الخلق والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting al-Khāliq for an hour or more in the middle of the night is said to illuminate the reciter's heart and face.
rows.anchor: وخاصية هذا الاسم أن يذكر في جوف الليل ساعة فما فوقها فيتنور قلب ذاكره ووجهه

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: The Idrīsī invocation calls God creator of all in the heavens and earth; al-Suhrawardī prescribes 5,000 recitations for recovering lost things or reaching an absent person far away.
rows.anchor: وفي الأربعين الإدريسية خالق من في السموات ومن في الأرض وكل إليه معاده قال السهروردي يذكر لجمع الضائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bāriʾ originates things without disparity or deficiency, in accord with wise measure and complete benefit.
rows.anchor: الموجد للأشياء بريئة من التفاوت فإن البرء الإيجاد على وجه يكون الموجد بريئا من التفاوت والنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant of al-Bāriʾ makes work balanced and consistent, doing what fits the divine name; the source connects this to the absence of disparity in God's creation.
rows.anchor: وعبد البارىء هو الذي يبرأ عمله من التفاوت والاختلاف فلا يفعل إلا ما يناسب حضرة الاسم البارىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting al-Bāriʾ one hundred times daily for seven consecutive days is prescribed for protection from afflictions, even in the grave.
rows.anchor: وخاصية هذا الاسم أن يذكره سبعة أيام متوالية كل يوم مائة مرة للسلامة من الآفات

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says the Idrīsī invocation to al-Bāriʾ opens wealth, honor, and safety from afflictions; writing the invocation on pitch and hanging it on a mad person or someone with a severe illness is said to help.
rows.anchor: قال السهروردي يفتح لذاكره أبواب الغنى والعز والسلامة من الآفات وإذا كتب في لوح من قير وعلق على المجنون نفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muṣawwir brings the forms and qualities of things into existence as He wills; He gives every created thing its form.
rows.anchor: الموجد لصور الأشياء وكيفياتها كما أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names are most beautiful because they indicate beautiful meanings, as discussed earlier in Sūrat Ṭā Hā.
rows.anchor: لدلالتها على المعاني الحسنة كما سبق في سورة طه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī says God's names are beautiful by the standards of both revelation and reason.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : مر اوراست نامهاى نيكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine superlative of al-aḥsan, just as al-ʿulyā is feminine for al-aʿlā.
rows.anchor: والحسنى صيغة تفضيل لأنها تأنيث الأحسن كالعليا في تأنيث الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the names absolutely most beautiful signifies unsurpassed excellence: God's names and essence have no comparison with the names or essences of others.
rows.anchor: وتوصيف الأسماء بها للزيادة المطلقة إذ لا نسبة لأسمائه إلى غير الأسماء من أسماء الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith gives God's names as ninety-nine.
rows.anchor: وأسماء الله تسعة وتسعون على ما جاء في الحديث

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says he saw a dhikr book listing four thousand names: a thousand each in the Qurʾān and sound reports, Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
rows.anchor: ونقل صاحب اللباب عن الإمام الرازي أنه قال : رأيت في بعض كتب الذكر

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet's supplication invokes every name God used for Himself, revealed in a book, taught to a creature, or reserved in knowledge of the unseen; the author suggests ninety-nine names are the best-known and most comprehensive.
rows.anchor: روي إن من دعاء رسول الله عليه السلام : أسألك بكل اسم سميت به نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The multiplicity of names does not entail multiple named beings: one person may be called father, grandfather, uncle, or scholar from different relations while remaining one.
rows.anchor: وتعدد الأسماء لا يدل على تعدد المسمى لأن الواحد يسمى أبا من وجه وجدا من وجه وخالا

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن البسطامي
rows.claim: Al-Bisṭāmī describes a retreat practice of taking the abjad value of a divine name, omitting the definite article, and reciting that exact number in a quiet place under the conditions of retreat to obtain a timely response.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن البسطامي قدس سره في ترويح القلوب : اعلم أن من السر المكتوم في الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that exceeding the prescribed number is waste and falling short is a defect; a name's count is like a key's teeth, opening the door of answered prayer.
rows.anchor: فإن الزيادة على العدد المطلوب إسراف والنقص منه إخلال والعدد في الذكر بالأسماء كأسنان المفتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowers attend to the article and the word's root in divine names, while the Malāmiyya omit the article as an addition beyond the root.
rows.anchor: ثم اعلم أن العارفين يلاحظون في الأسماء آلة التعريف وأصل الكلمة والملامية يطرحون منها آلة التعريف

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars define a name as a conventional expression for a meaning, the named as that meaning, and naming as assigning or applying the expression.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء : الاسم هو اللفظ الدال على المعنى بالوضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars hold that naming God is restricted to terms found in the Qurʾān or an authentic hadith.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الاسم على الله تعالى توقفي عند البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other scholars allow any term whose meaning befits God's majesty.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : كل لفظ دل على معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictive view cites God's established descriptions as ʿĀlim, ʿAlīm, and ʿAllām, while rejecting unattested terms such as ʿĀrif, Faqīh, and Mutayaqqin.
rows.anchor: ومن أدلة الأولين أن الله عالم بلا مرية فيقال له عالم وعليم وعلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permissive view argues that Muslim consensus accepts fitting descriptions in Persian, Turkish, and Indian, even though those words are absent from scripture.
rows.anchor: ومن أدلة الآخرين أن الأسماءوصفاته مذكورة بالفارسية والتركية والهندية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permissive view invokes 17:110: God commands people to call on Him by the most beautiful names, which are beautiful because they denote perfect attributes; meaning, not the wording alone, is decisive.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن الله تعالى قال : ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها والاسم لا يحسن إلا لدلالته على صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A newly coined term that suggests an unsuitable meaning is discourteous, but a term conveying a sound, beautiful meaning without a repugnant implication is not disrespectful.
rows.anchor: غاية ما في الباب أن يكون وضع الاسم علما له مستحدثا

words: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Jumuʿa is Medinan and has eleven verses.
rows.anchor: إحدى عشرة آية مدنية

words: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All that is in the heavens and earth, animate or inanimate, continually glorifies God; the upper realm's wonders and lower realm's beings are related to Him through life and praise.
rows.anchor: جميعا من حي وجامد تسبيحا مستمرة فما في السموات هي البدائع العلوية وما في الأرض هي الكوائين السفلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik is the everlasting sovereign, al-Quddūs is free of defect, al-ʿAzīz prevails over whatever He wills, and al-Ḥakīm possesses wondrous and far-reaching wisdom.
rows.anchor: ادشاهى كه ملك او دائمست وبى زوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority parse al-Malik and the following names as genitive adjectives describing God's name.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على جر الملك وما بعده على أنها صفات لاسم الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra opens with glorification because it mentions the Messenger's mission, which presupposes a guide for the world, disputes the Jews' claim to be God's children and beloved, and closes with people abandoning remembrance to hear a sermon of prayer, praise, and glorification.
rows.anchor: بدأ الله تعالى هذه السورة بالتسبيح لما فيها من ذكر البعثة إذا خلاء العالم من المرشد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the verse as declaring God's sacred essence transcendent.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية يعني ينزه ذاته المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is from the unlettered people's own community and lineage, an Arab and unlettered like them.
rows.anchor: أي من جملتهم ونسبهم عربيا أميا مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His likeness to them is a favor: it shows he did not learn from books, while they knew his lineage and circumstances.
rows.anchor: فوجه الامتنان مشاكلة حاله لأحوالهم ونفي التعلم من الكتب

rows.speaker: شعيا عليه السلام
rows.claim: The book of Isaiah is quoted as foretelling that God would send an unlettered messenger among the unlettered and seal the prophets through him.
rows.anchor: ودر كتاب شعيا عليه السلام مذكور است كه انى ابعث أميا في الأميين واختم به النبيين

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī's three Persian couplets praise the Prophet's unletteredness: God named him unlettered though he received the Mother of the Book, and without schooling he revealed the Tablet's secrets; the final couplet's wording is corrupt.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : ودر اميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being sent among the unlettered does not limit the Prophet's universal mission; even if it implied a restriction, the explicit statement that he was sent to all people overrides it, refuting the People of the Book's claim that he was only for Arabs.
rows.anchor: والبعث في الأميين لا ينافي عموم دعوته عليه السلام فالتخصيص بالذكر لا مفهوم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger recites the Qurʾān to them despite being unlettered and having no prior practice in reading or learning; tilāwa is sequential recitation like study or regular litanies, while qirāʾa more broadly means voicing letters.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين التلاوة والقرآن أن التلاوة قراءة القرآن متتابعة كالدراسة والأوراد المظفة والقراءة أعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As another attribute of the Messenger, he leads people to become pure of corrupt beliefs and deeds.
rows.anchor: صفة أخرى لرسولا معطوفة على يتلو أي يحملهم على ما يصيرون به أزكياء من خبائث العقائد والأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This signals the Sufi path: God is the true purifier, yet the Perfect Human manifests divine attributes; the source supports this with 4:49 and 4:80.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى قاعدة التسليك فإن المزكي في الحقيقة وإن كان هو الله تعالى كما قال بل الله يزكي من يشاء

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād says teaching follows recitation in existence, with purification placed between them because it perfects the practical soul after recitation perfects the theoretical faculty through knowledge; this ordering shows that each benefit is a distinct bounty deserving thanks.
rows.anchor: قال في الإرشاد صفة أخرى لرسولا مترتبة في الوجود على التلاوة وإنما وسط بينهما التزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain the Book and Wisdom as the Qurʾān and the revealed law, or as its wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ويعلمهم القرآن والشريعة وهي ما شرع الله لعباده من الأحكام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets them as the Qurʾān and Sunna.
rows.anchor: أو القرآن والسنة كما قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the Book as writing.
rows.anchor: أو الكتاب الخط كما قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq interprets the Book as knowledge of good and evil.
rows.anchor: أو الخير والشر كما قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik interprets Wisdom as jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: والحكمة الفقه كما قاله مالك

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash interprets Wisdom as exhortation.
rows.anchor: أو العظة كما قاله الأعمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms also encompass the legal rulings of the Sharīʿa and the refined practices of the spiritual path, with their combined wisdom.
rows.anchor: أو كتاب أحكام الشريعة وأسرار آداب الطريقة وحاصل معانيه الحكمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān's realities and wisdom are taught fully to people of understanding, including select Companions and later generations; the Prophet taught Companions directly and later believers through the community's perfected inheritors.
rows.anchor: ولكن تعليم حقائق القرآن وحكمه مختص بأولى الفهم وهم خواص الأصحاب رضي الله عنهم وخواص التابعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's teaching of the Qurʾān's realities and wisdom would alone suffice as a miracle.
rows.anchor: ولو لم يكن سوى هذا التعليم معجزة لكفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Būṣī's Burda line says the Prophet's knowledge while unlettered in the age of ignorance is sufficient evidence of his miracle, as is his instruction in manners while an orphan.
rows.anchor: كفاك بالعلم في الأمي معجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In is the lightened emphatic particle, not conditional or negative; the lām marks the difference from a negative construction.
rows.anchor: إن ليست شرطية ولا نافية بل هي المخففة واللام هر الفارقة بينها وبين النافية

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Prophet's mission the unlettered people were in manifest error through idolatry and the impurities of the pre-Islamic age; this shows their need for a guide and rebuts the idea that he learned from them.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وأن الشأن كان الأميون من قبل بعثته ومجيئه لفي ضلال مبين من الشرك وخبث الجاهلية

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī says attributing error to everyone is by predominance, since Waraqa b. Nawfal, Zayd b. ʿAmr, and Quss b. Sāʿida were guided and, according to the Prophet, each would be raised as a community alone.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : والظاهر أن نسبة الكون في الضلال إلى الجميع من باب التغليب

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that qualification: those men were guided in monotheism but remained astray concerning revealed laws and rulings; being guided in one respect does not conflict with error in another.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : هو اعتراض على معنى الإزاحة المذكورة لكنه ليس بشيء فإن اهتداء من ذكره

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites 93:7 but says it does not imply the Prophet ever committed idolatry or other sins; recitation and instruction gave purification and rescue from error in its full sense.
rows.anchor: فقد كانوا في ضلال من الشرائع والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ākharīn is the plural of ākhir in the sense of “others” and can be coordinated with “the unlettered,” referring to later unlettered Arabs.
rows.anchor: جمع آخر بمعنى غير وهو عطف على الأميين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “others” coordinates with the object of “teaches”: he teaches them and others from among them.
rows.anchor: أو على المنصوب في يعلمهم أي يعلمهم ويعلم آخرين منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may refer to others like the Arabs in language and unletteredness; if non-Arabs are intended, “from among them” attaches directly to “others.”
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد العجم فمنهم يكون متعلقا بآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the first view as more imposing and expressive of power: four supports like those of the Kaaba correspond to four heart pillars—spirit, secret, self, and nature—and outward plus inward aspects yield eight thousands.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : الأنسب هو الأول لكونه أدخل في العظمة والهيبة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the passage as the Essence bearing eight essential unseen attributes, keys to the unseen, while the attributes bear their own manifestations.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : يشير إلى عشر الذات الحاملة للصفات الثمانية الذاتية الغيبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “you are presented” governs “that day”; presentation means being brought before God for questioning and accounting, like a ruler reviewing troops, and the address covers everyone by predominance.
rows.anchor: على الله أي تسألون وتحاسبون عبر عنه بذلك تشبيها له بعرض السلطان العسكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes three presentations on Judgment Day: two involve excuses, arguments, and rebuke, while the third distributes the records, with the successful receiving their book in the right hand and the doomed in the left.
rows.anchor: أن في يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فاعتذار واحتجاج وتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although presentation follows the second trumpet, “the Day” spans the trumpet blasts, swoon, resurrection, reckoning, and entry into Paradise or Hell, so it can serve as the time for them all.
rows.anchor: لكن لما كان اليوماسما لزمان متسع يقع فيه النفختان والصعقة والنشور

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: The anthropomorphists take the references to the Throne's bearing and the presentation to mean that God is carried and present on the Throne.
rows.anchor: وذهب المشبهة من حمل العرش والعرض إلى كونه تعالى محمولا حاضرا في العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that the imagery depicts God's majesty by comparison with rulers presiding over judgment; God's coming amid clouds means the coming of His command and decree.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه تمثل لعظمة الله بما يشاهد من أحوال السلاطين يوم بروزهم للقضاء العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author interprets the report of transformation as God's manifestation in an attribute-rank; the Prophet's vision of a beardless youth during the Ascension is like a dream vision, since God is exalted beyond bodily qualities.
rows.anchor: وأما حديث التحول فمحمول على ظهوره تعالى في مرتبة الصفت ولا مناقشة فيه لأن النبي عليه اسلام رآه ليلة المعراج في صورة شاب امرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause is circumstantial to “you are presented”; min-kum originally modified khāfiya but was fronted for the rhyme, and it syntactically reaches both the preceding and following wording.
rows.anchor: حال من مرفوع تعرضون ومنكم كان في الأصل صفة لخافية قدم للفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presentation exposes every hidden secret and displays the state to emphasize justice; the source compares it with 82:9, “the day the secrets are tested.”
rows.anchor: أي تعرضون غير خاف عليه تعالى فعلة خفيفة أي سر من أسراركم وإنما العرض لإفشاء الحال والمبالغة في العدل
